title: India must embrace future technologies, lead world in creating them: PM Modi
excerpt: New Delhi, Oct 27: India must embrace future technologies, innovate boldly and lead the world in developing them, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Tuesday and asserted that the country is moving forward with a new mindset and a newfound self-confidence in the field of science and technology. Addressing the Emerging Science, Technology and Innovation Conclave (ESTIC)-2026 here, he also said the country’s goal is to create new technology and shape its direction — for India, for the world, for today, and for tomorrow. “India must embrace technology of the future, innovate boldly, and lead the world in creating them,” Modi said. "Today, 21st-century India is moving forward with a new mindset and a newfound self-confidence,” he said. During his address, the prime minister highlighted that from the discovery of zero to the development of the number system and advancements in astronomy, India’s culture has always been rooted in knowledge and discovery. The country is currently carrying this scientific heritage forward with modern technology and renewed confidence, he said. Speaking about nuclear energy, he stated that building a Viksit Bharat requires nuclear energy on a large scale, and that’s why India is developing fast breeder reactor technology. The prime minister noted that it was a significant milestone when the country’s first indigenous prototype fast breeder reactor (PFBR) in Kalpakkam, Tamil Nadu, attained criticality in August this year. Modi also said the country’s successes achieved across different sectors are unprecedented. For instance, first shipments of chips made in India have now started reaching the world, he said. “In the field of battery storage as well, we are working on capacity building using what is available in India,” said the prime minister. Underlining the milestone achieved in the space sector, Modi said the July mission of Indian firm Skyroot Aerospace, which involved the launch of the country’s first privately developed orbital rocket Vikram-1, and placing of multiple technology demonstration payloads in low Earth orbit. “From nuclear to space, from AI to semiconductors... The needs of all these sectors are different, but the message from all of them is the same. India is enhancing both its strength and its confidence in emerging technologies,” said Modi.

title: Ahmedabad gets 19 bomb threats in a day, schools among key targets
excerpt: Ahmedabad, October 27 (IANS): Nineteen bomb threat messages targeting schools, courts, Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation (AMC) offices and the Narendra Modi Stadium were received on Tuesday, a cybercrime branch official confirmed to IANS, as security agencies responded to threatening emails sent to educational institutions and other locations in the city. Of the 19 threats reported until the time of confirmation, 14 concerned schools, two targeted courts, two referred to the AMC or the Mayor’s Office, and one concerned the Narendra Modi Stadium. One of the emails, received by Shree Narayana Guru School, carried the subject line “Warning! BOM|B Blast Ahmedabad Schools @ 1:11 PM”.The email was sent at 9:10 a.m. from an account identified as (reduak079@gmail.com) and addressed to three school email accounts, including those of C.N. Vidyavihar and Shree Narayana Guru School. The message contained threats of bomb blasts at specified times and referred to schools, courts, an office and the Narendra Modi Stadium. It also warned people against travelling to Motera Stadium Metro station on November 21, the date mentioned in connection with Punjabi singer Diljit Dosanjh’s scheduled concert at the stadium. The email included the slogans “KHALISTAN Zindabad” and “KHOON ka BADLA KHOON da” and purported to invoke the name of the Khalistan National Army. It also referred to Babbar Khalsa and named several individuals. The authenticity of these claims and the identity of the sender have not been independently established. The message further warned recipients against picking up iPhones found on roads, claiming that the devices could be used to cause explosions. It also threatened blasts at schools and other locations, giving specific times for the alleged attacks. The threats prompted security checks at affected locations. Local police, bomb detection teams and dog squads were deployed at schools, with school authorities taking precautionary measures, including sending students home and asking parents to collect them. The AMC headquarters was evacuated after a bomb threat. A thorough check was conducted at the targeted places. The latest incident follows previous bomb threats against public institutions and prominent venues in Gujarat. The investigation into threats in Ahmedabad is under way, with the sender’s identity and the credibility of the messages yet to be established.

title: Ahmedabad couple started 'The Coco Station', selling home-made cold cocoa & cold coffee; made ₹36 lakh in 1.5 yr
excerpt: In modern-day India, more people are willing to take risks and put in the extra hustle to build something of their own. Even after a full day of work, they find the energy to grow a venture that could one day free them from depending on a salary. One such couple is Ahmedabad-based Darshan Zinzuvadiya and Shruti Zinzuvadiya, who started The Coco Station in July 2025. Darshan works as a software engineer, while Shruti quit her job as the business grew. Every night from 9:00 PM to 12:00 AM, once Darshan is back from the office, the couple sell cold cocoa and cold coffee from their car. “Initially, we were hesitant, but we decided to put our doubts aside and start the business. We prepare everything in the morning, from cleaning the equipment and filling the ice box to mixing the ingredients. Once I return from work, we head out to sell our drinks from 9 PM to midnight,” Darshan Zinzuvadiya told Startup Pedia in an exclusive interview. About Darshan Zinzuvadiya & Shruti Zinzuvadiya Currently, Darshan Zinzuvadiya and Shruti Zinzuvadiya are a 26-year-old couple living in Ahmedabad, Gujarat. Darshan, a native of Jamnagar district, Gujarat, completed his Bachelor of Engineering in Communication from Gujarat Technological University in 2021. He currently works as a software engineer at a tech company in Gujarat. Shruti, a native of Savarkundla, District Amreli, Gujarat, completed her BBA from Saurashtra University in 2018-19 and her MBA in Finance from Gujarat University in 2021. Darshan and Shruti got married in 2025. Before marriage, Shruti worked at an accounting firm for one year between 2024 and 2025. After marriage, she continued working there as a Business Development Executive for 3-4 months. She left her corporate job as her venture began to grow. “In the earlier stage, I was managing both my job and this business. But it became quite difficult, because sales increased, demand increased, and so did the responsibility. It was hard to manage everything, so I had to quit my job,” Shruti told Startup Pedia. Earlier Experience in Business Long before starting The Coco Station, Darshan and Shruti had tried their hands at business separately. While working as a software engineer, Darshan and his friends started a dropshipping business. Within just 15 days, they were receiving around 30 orders per day. Darshan continued managing the business alongside his IT job. Shruti, on the other hand, started a small business with her friends during her BBA. They made and sold handmade jewellery and handicrafts to fellow students and some professors at their college. She continued this for around 3 years, which gave her some experience in making and selling products. Both had some experience with business, but neither had a clear idea of what business to start next. “I personally didn’t know much about the business and startup world. After the dropshipping venture failed, I started watching Shark Tank India and reading business and startup articles online, which helped me build a strong foundation in business and sales,” Darshan says. How Darshan and Shruti Started The Coco Station Shruti had learnt to make a cold cocoa drink at home using cocoa powder, sugar, and milk. One Saturday, she made this drink for their friends, who had visited the couple for a casual meetup. Fortunately, their friends liked the drink and suggested that the couple try selling it as a business. “Our friends are very supportive and encouraging. They already knew what we were thinking of, and when they suggested that we start a business around cold cocoa drink, we appreciated their suggestion and started it,” Shruti says. The very next day, Shruti prepared around 14 bottles of chilled cocoa drink using the same recipe she had learnt at home. The couple then went outside their house to sell the drink. They put up a banner indicating what they were offering. Within 40-45 minutes, all 14 bottles were sold at Rs 80 per bottle. That day, the couple earned Rs 1,120. All the customers liked the drink and encouraged them to continue selling it. Growth through social media According to Shruti, people in Ahmedabad are kind and encouraging towards young people starting their own businesses. When the couple started selling cocoa coffee on the first day, they did not face any resistance or backlash. Instead, people encouraged them to continue, which gave the couple a morale boost. Darshan and Shruti then created an Instagram page to promote their day-to-day operations and products. Word of mouth also played a major role in popularising The Coco Station in Ahmedabad. According to the founders, they do not use preservatives or artificial flavours in their products, which gives their drinks a distinct, homemade taste. Menu & Pricing The Coco Station initially launched its cold cocoa drink in July 2025 and later added cold coffee in response to customer demand. According to the founders, they prepare their cold coffee using pure coffee, Amul Gold milk, and sugar, without using powders or chemicals. The cold cocoa menu includes toppings such as choco chips, KitKat, Oreo, Biscoff, and dry fruits. They also offer a Two-in-One option that combines choco chips with dry fruits. The plain cold cocoa is priced at Rs 100, while other flavours are also priced at Rs 100, with additional charges for toppings. The Coco Station Special costs Rs 160. The drinks are served in 300 ml bottles filled with 265 ml of the beverage. Investment and Challenges The Coco Station started with an investment of around Rs 2,000-3,000. According to the couple, the business has been running on its own earnings ever since. Today, running the business costs around Rs 1.5-2 lakh per month, including expenses on raw materials, bottles, and other operating costs. The couple buys cocoa powder, sugar, and milk fresh every day. However, the couple has faced several challenges while running the business. One of the main challenges is the lack of space and infrastructure. Since they operate from a car, the limited space in its trunk restricts the machinery they can use. Daily routine of the Coco Station Founders The couple operates around 100 metres from their home, opposite Parivar Homes, Devnagar, Char Rasta, Gota, Ahmedabad. They sell their drinks every night from 9 PM to midnight. Every morning, Darshan gets ready for work after breakfast. Once he leaves for the office, Shruti starts preparing for the evening work. She cleans the equipment, organises the supplies, fills the ice box, and mixes the ingredients to prepare the drinks. She then fills around 150 bottles by hand for the day's sales and stores them in the refrigerator. After completing the preparations, she spends the afternoon attending to household chores. Once Darshan returns from work in the evening, the couple have dinner before heading to their selling spot to begin their nightly sales. On Sundays and holidays, the couple usually start selling earlier, at around 7 PM. Current Sales & Revenue The Coco Station initially sold around 14 bottles of cold cocoa on its first day in July 2025, earning approximately Rs 1,000. Over the next few months, their daily sales grew to around 42-50 bottles per day. Today, Darshan and Shruti sell around 150 bottles a day on average. The startup is now generating around Rs 20,000 in daily sales, which amounts to approximately Rs 6 lakh a month. The Coco Station has now crossed Rs 36 lakh in total revenue to date. Their sales have reached 30,000 bottles overall, including around 7,500 bottles sold in just 9 days during Navratri. The couple prepare their drinks in advance and keep buffer stock to meet demand, as the beverages have a shelf life of 2 days. Selling a Ready-to-Use Premix The Coco Station also sells a premix powder for people who want to start a similar business. The powder combines cocoa or coffee powder with sugar, already mixed. Buyers add 5 litres of milk to one 900 gm packet, blend it, and stir until the milk thickens. They then bring it to room temperature and store it in the refrigerator. Once chilled, the drink is ready to sell. One packet makes about 20 glasses of 250 ml each and is priced at around Rs 2,000-3,000. So far, they have sold around 2,000 kg of premix powder. The couple began selling the premix after receiving many inquiries, but say handling them every day is difficult. They plan to set up a manufacturing unit and then distribute through franchises. Future Goals The couple’s immediate goal is to move from the car to a proper outlet. They say they will open their first outlet in Ahmedabad shortly, and then grow city by city. In the next two years, they are thinking of 4-5 outlets, depending on how the public response goes. Their larger aim is to build a sustainable and profitable brand. FAQ Q. What is The Coco Station? A. The Coco Station is an Ahmedabad-based beverage business founded by Darshan Zinzuvadiya and Shruti Zinzuvadiya in July 2025. It sells cold cocoa, cold coffee, and premix powder. How much does The Coco Station earn? The Coco Station has crossed Rs 36 lakh in total sales, with daily sales of approximately Rs 20,000 and monthly sales of around Rs 6 lakh. How did Darshan and Shruti start The Coco Station? The couple started the business in July 2025 with an investment of around Rs 2,000-3,000 after friends encouraged them to sell the cold cocoa Shruti prepared at home. What are the future plans of The Coco Station? The couple plan to open their first outlet in Ahmedabad and expand to 4-5 outlets over the next two years

Its predecessor, the moto Edge 60 Neo, stood out as a compact upper mid-range phone, and the Edge 70 Neo is expected to follow suit. According to industry leaks, the Edge 70 Neo could feature a 50MP Sony LYTIA 710 main camera at the back, a 6.3-inch 1.5K OLED panel, and a MediaTek Dimensity 7450 chipset.
